title: Make a chart from your data
summary: Select data and insert a recommended column chart with a title.

steps.say: Make sure your Month and Amount data is on screen. Say done when ready.

checks.prompt: Are columns of months and amounts visible in the grid?

hints: Any two columns, one of labels and one of numbers, will work.
Go back to the first lesson to create the sample data.
steps.why: A chart needs labels and numbers to plot.

steps.say: Select A1 to B7, the headings and the six rows of data.

checks.prompt: Are cells A1 to B7 highlighted?

hints: Drag from A1 to B7. Leave out the total and average rows.
Type A1 colon B7 in the Name Box and press Enter.
steps.why: The chart uses whatever cells are selected.

steps.say: Click the Insert tab at the top.

checks.prompt: Is the Insert tab of the ribbon showing, with a Charts group?

hints: Insert is the tab right after Home.
Press Alt, then N, to open it with the keyboard.
steps.why: Charts, pictures and shapes are all added from Insert.

steps.say: Click Recommended Charts, then pick a column chart and click OK.

checks.prompt: Is a chart now visible on the sheet?

hints: Recommended Charts is in the Charts group. The first suggestion is usually a column chart.
Press Alt and F1 to drop a default chart straight onto the sheet.
steps.why: Recommended Charts shows previews so you can choose by eye.

steps.say: Check that a chart appeared on the sheet. Say done when you see it.

checks.prompt: Is there a chart with bars for each month on the sheet?

hints: It appears over the grid, near your data.
If nothing appeared, select the data again and press Alt and F1.
steps.why: Seeing the chart confirms it used the right cells.

steps.say: Click the chart title, select its text, and type Amount by month.

checks.prompt: Does the chart title now read Amount by month?

hints: Click the title once to select the box, then again to edit the text.
Use Chart Elements, the plus button next to the chart, to turn the title on if it is missing.
steps.why: A clear title tells readers what the chart shows.

steps.say: Drag the chart by its edge so it doesn't cover your data. Control Z undoes a move.

checks.prompt: Is the chart positioned so it no longer covers cells A1 to B9?

hints: Grab the chart border, not the bars or the title.
On Chart Design, click Move Chart and choose New sheet.
steps.why: With data and chart both visible, you can watch the chart follow your edits.
